source_reconciliation.finding: The web Sanskrit witnesses do not expose the same complete verse sequence as the printed Dīpikā edition. Wikisource jumps from verse 8 to 10 and from 34 to 36; BharatKosha's printed commentary explicitly reaches verse 50 and contains additional material on dravya, guṇa, vīrya, vipāka, prabhāva, ṛtu and doṣa dynamics.
source_reconciliation.critical_rule: Do not fill missing verses by inference or by renumbering a different witness. Preserve source numbering and reconcile the printed Sanskrit before creating final śloka records.
source_reconciliation.confirmed_printed_end: Verse 50 is the kapha-prakopa/prashama conclusion, followed by the Bhaiṣajyākhyānaka colophon.
source_reconciliation.commentary_author: Dr. Brahmānanda Tripāṭhī, Dīpikā commentary and special explanatory notes in the BharatKosha/Chaukhamba witness.
